text.brief: On December 17, 1943, Franklin Roosevelt signed the law that ended sixty-one years of Chinese exclusion.
text.record: Japanese propaganda cited the exclusion laws to tell Chinese audiences that their American ally despised them. Roosevelt asked Congress to repeal the laws as a war measure, and the Magnuson Act allowed Chinese immigrants to naturalize. It set a quota of 105 entries a year.
text.reading: Repeal answered an enemy's information operation by removing its true material. The move echoes Emancipation, a coherence move that closed a door the adversary had pried open, and it cost little because the quota stayed token.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The ally's own statute supplied the enemy's best propaganda for a decade.
text.fix: Audit the statute book for grievances an adversary can quote, and fix them before the adversary uses them.
